name: 6-Hour SQL Brush-Up
blurb: Not a course — a sharpening. Six focused hours that compress the full foundation into a fast, drill-heavy refresh on the ShopNow tables. Attempt every drill first, then reveal.

hours.title: Filtering, CASE & Data Profiling
hours.recap: SELECT … FROM … WHERE … ORDER BY … LIMIT; CASE WHEN … THEN … ELSE … END; the difference between COUNT(*), COUNT(col), COUNT(DISTINCT col); COALESCE, NULLIF. Profiling = interrogating a table before you trust it.

drills.q: Profile orders in one query: total rows, distinct customers, distinct products, earliest & latest order date.
drills.answer:
SELECT
  COUNT(*)                   AS rows,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) AS distinct_customers,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ProductID)  AS distinct_products,
  MIN(OrderDate)             AS first_order,
  MAX(OrderDate)             AS last_order
FROM orders;

drills.q: Count orders by OrderStatus and show each status as a % of all orders.
drills.answer:
SELECT OrderStatus, COUNT(*) AS orders,
  ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders), 1) AS pct_of_total
FROM orders
GROUP BY OrderStatus
ORDER BY orders DESC;
drills.note: Note the 100.0 — integer division would truncate the percentage to 0.

drills.q: Bucket every order's ShippingDays into 'Fast (<=2)', 'Normal (3-5)', 'Slow (>5)' and count each bucket.
drills.answer:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN ShippingDays <= 2 THEN 'Fast (<=2)'
       WHEN ShippingDays <= 5 THEN 'Normal (3-5)'
       ELSE 'Slow (>5)' END AS ship_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY MIN(ShippingDays);

drills.q: Find the 'impossible' rows: orders where Revenue <= 0 OR ShippingDays < 0. How many are there?
Compute a NULL-safe margin % per order: GrossProfit / Revenue * 100 without dividing by zero.
drills.answer:
SELECT OrderID,
  ROUND(GrossProfit / NULLIF(Revenue, 0) * 100, 2) AS margin_pct
FROM orders
LIMIT 20;
drills.note: NULLIF(Revenue,0) turns a 0 denominator into NULL, so the result is NULL instead of an error.

hours.title: Aggregation, HAVING & Conditional Aggregation
hours.recap: GROUP BY sets the grain; HAVING filters groups after aggregation; SUM(CASE WHEN … THEN … ELSE 0 END) computes many measures in one pass. The most important pattern in the whole brush-up.

drills.q: Total revenue and order count by Category, highest revenue first.
drills.answer:
SELECT Category, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(Revenue), 0) AS revenue
FROM orders
GROUP BY Category
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

drills.q: Only categories with more than 5,000 orders.
drills.answer:
SELECT Category, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY Category
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5000
ORDER BY orders DESC;
drills.note: WHERE can't see COUNT(*) — group-level filters belong in HAVING.

drills.q: In ONE query per category: gross revenue, net revenue (returns = 0), and the rupees lost to returns.
drills.answer:
SELECT Category,
  ROUND(SUM(Revenue), 0) AS gross_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN 0 ELSE Revenue END), 0) AS net_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN Revenue ELSE 0 END), 0) AS lost_to_returns
FROM orders
GROUP BY Category
ORDER BY net_revenue DESC;

drills.q: Return rate (% of orders returned) by category, worst first.
drills.answer:
SELECT Category, COUNT(*) AS orders,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS return_rate_pct
FROM orders
GROUP BY Category
ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC;

drills.q: Average order value (AOV) by OrderYear, excluding returns and non-positive revenue.
drills.answer:
SELECT OrderYear, ROUND(AVG(Revenue), 0) AS aov
FROM orders
WHERE ReturnFlag='No' AND Revenue > 0
GROUP BY OrderYear
ORDER BY OrderYear;

hours.title: Joins, Anti-Joins & Set Operations
hours.recap: INNER keeps matches only; LEFT keeps all left rows (unmatched → NULL on the right); the LEFT JOIN … WHERE right.key IS NULL pattern finds what's missing; UNION stacks result sets. In this dataset, the unmatched rows are usually the point.

drills.q: Revenue by Brand (top 10). Brand lives in products.
drills.answer:
SELECT p.Brand, ROUND(SUM(o.Revenue), 0) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN products p ON o.ProductID = p.ProductID
GROUP BY p.Brand
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 10;

drills.q: How many orders reference a ProductID that doesn't exist in products (deprecated SKUs)? Use a LEFT JOIN.
drills.answer:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_on_deprecated_skus, ROUND(SUM(o.Revenue), 0) AS revenue_affected
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN products p ON o.ProductID = p.ProductID
WHERE p.ProductID IS NULL;
drills.note: This is exactly the revenue an INNER JOIN would have silently dropped.

drills.q: How many orders have no matching row in payments? (anti-join)
drills.answer:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS unpaid_orders
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN payments pmt ON o.OrderID = pmt.OrderID
WHERE pmt.OrderID IS NULL;
drills.sparkNote: Databricks also supports the explicit form: FROM orders o LEFT ANTI JOIN payments pmt ON o.OrderID = pmt.OrderID. DuckDB uses the LEFT JOIN … IS NULL pattern (or ANTI JOIN).

drills.q: Revenue by customer Region. (Heads-up: raw customers has duplicate IDs — note the risk; you fix it in S1.)
drills.answer:
SELECT c.Region, ROUND(SUM(o.Revenue), 0) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
GROUP BY c.Region
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
drills.note: Because customers has ~120 duplicate IDs, those customers' orders are counted twice here. In the internship you always join to customers_clean instead.

drills.q: Rehearse UNION/DISTINCT: list distinct Region and distinct State stacked with a label.
drills.answer:
SELECT 'Region' AS field, Region AS value FROM customers WHERE Region IS NOT NULL
UNION
SELECT 'State', State FROM customers
ORDER BY field, value;
drills.note: UNION de-duplicates; UNION ALL keeps every row (and is faster when you don't need de-dup).

hours.title: Subqueries & CTEs
hours.recap: A scalar subquery returns one value; IN (subquery) filters by a set; a correlated subquery references the outer row; a WITH (CTE) names a step so the query reads like an argument. Prefer CTEs over deep nesting.

drills.q: Orders whose revenue is above the overall average order revenue.
drills.answer:
SELECT OrderID, Revenue
FROM orders
WHERE Revenue > (SELECT AVG(Revenue) FROM orders)
ORDER BY Revenue DESC
LIMIT 20;

drills.q: Using a CTE: categories whose total revenue is above the average category revenue.
drills.answer:
WITH cat_rev AS (
  SELECT Category, SUM(Revenue) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY Category
)
SELECT Category, ROUND(revenue, 0) AS revenue
FROM cat_rev
WHERE revenue > (SELECT AVG(revenue) FROM cat_rev)
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

drills.q: Correlated subquery: products priced above their own category's average SellingPrice.
drills.note: The inner query re-runs per outer row, scoped to that row's category — that's 'correlated.'

drills.q: How many customers have at least one returned order? Use IN.
CTE chain: bucket customers by lifetime order count (1, 2-3, 4-5, 6+) and count customers per bucket.
drills.answer:
WITH cust_orders AS (
  SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY CustomerID
)
SELECT CASE WHEN n=1 THEN '1' WHEN n<=3 THEN '2-3' WHEN n<=5 THEN '4-5' ELSE '6+' END AS order_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM cust_orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY MIN(n);

hours.title: Window Functions
hours.recap: A window function keeps every row and computes across a frame: ROW_NUMBER/RANK/DENSE_RANK, LAG/LEAD, and aggregates like SUM() OVER (…). The engine is OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY o). The dividing line between intermediate and senior SQL.

drills.q: Number each customer's orders in date order (1 = first ever order).
drills.answer:
SELECT OrderID, CustomerID, OrderDate,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate) AS order_seq
FROM orders
ORDER BY CustomerID, order_seq
LIMIT 50;

drills.q: Top 3 products by revenue within each category.
drills.answer:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT Category, ProductID, SUM(Revenue) AS revenue,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Category ORDER BY SUM(Revenue) DESC) AS rn
  FROM orders GROUP BY Category, ProductID
)
SELECT Category, rn, ProductID, ROUND(revenue, 0) AS revenue
FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY Category, rn;

drills.q: Monthly revenue with the previous month's revenue beside it (LAG).
drills.answer:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT OrderYear, OrderMonth, SUM(Revenue) AS rev FROM orders GROUP BY OrderYear, OrderMonth
)
SELECT OrderYear, OrderMonth, ROUND(rev, 0) AS revenue,
  ROUND(LAG(rev) OVER (ORDER BY OrderYear, OrderMonth), 0) AS prev_month
FROM monthly
ORDER BY OrderYear, OrderMonth;

drills.q: Add a cumulative running total of revenue to that monthly series.
drills.answer:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT OrderYear, OrderMonth, SUM(Revenue) AS rev FROM orders GROUP BY OrderYear, OrderMonth
)
SELECT OrderYear, OrderMonth, ROUND(rev, 0) AS revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(rev) OVER (ORDER BY OrderYear, OrderMonth), 0) AS running_total
FROM monthly
ORDER BY OrderYear, OrderMonth;

drills.q: Explain the difference between ROW_NUMBER, RANK, and DENSE_RANK on tied values.
drills.answer:
-- For values 100, 100, 90:
-- ROW_NUMBER -> 1, 2, 3 (arbitrary tiebreak, always unique)
-- RANK       -> 1, 1, 3 (ties share a rank, then a gap)
-- DENSE_RANK -> 1, 1, 2 (ties share, no gap)
-- 'Exactly top N rows' -> ROW_NUMBER; 'everyone tied at the top' -> RANK/DENSE_RANK.

hours.title: Dialect Specifics + Speed Round
hours.recap: The app runs DuckDB; the internship's 'production' environment is Databricks/Spark SQL. These are the idioms that differ — learn both forms.

drills.q: Median product Rating per category.
drills.answer:
SELECT Category, median(Rating) AS median_rating
FROM products
GROUP BY Category
ORDER BY median_rating DESC;
drills.sparkNote: Spark: percentile_approx(Rating, 0.5). DuckDB: median(Rating) or quantile_cont(Rating, 0.5).

drills.q: Deduplicate customers to one row per ID (latest JoinDate) using QUALIFY.
drills.note: QUALIFY filters on a window result without a wrapping subquery — supported in both DuckDB and Databricks.

drills.q: Standardize a dirty city value: '  MUMBAI ' → 'Mumbai'.
drills.answer:
-- DuckDB has no INITCAP; lower+trim gives 'mumbai':
SELECT TRIM(LOWER('  MUMBAI ')) AS clean;
drills.sparkNote: Spark: INITCAP(TRIM(LOWER('  MUMBAI '))) -> 'Mumbai'. DuckDB lacks INITCAP — normalize to lower+trim (the distinct count is identical; only display casing differs).

drills.q: Days between each order and the latest order in the table.
drills.answer:
SELECT OrderID,
  date_diff('day', OrderDate, (SELECT MAX(OrderDate) FROM orders)) AS days_before_latest
FROM orders
LIMIT 20;
drills.sparkNote: Spark: DATEDIFF(end, start) -> days. DuckDB: date_diff('day', start, end) (note argument order) or simply (end - start) for DATE columns.

drills.q: Build a '2024-03' style month label from OrderDate. (Heads-up: OrderMonth is already stored as 'YYYY-MM' and OrderQuarter as 'Q1-2022' — profile columns before assuming their type.)
drills.answer:
SELECT strftime(OrderDate, '%Y-%m') AS month_label
FROM orders LIMIT 5;
drills.sparkNote: Spark: DATE_FORMAT(OrderDate,'yyyy-MM'). DuckDB: strftime(OrderDate,'%Y-%m'). And note ShopNow's OrderMonth column is already a 'YYYY-MM' string, so you can often just use it directly.

diagnostic.title: Entry Diagnostic — "The Offer Letter"
diagnostic.intro: Ten questions, closed-book. Write runnable SQL against the ShopNow tables. Pass bar: 8/10. The four auto-graded questions must match exactly; the rest reveal a model answer to self-mark. A query only counts if it runs AND is correct on edge cases (guard divide-by-zero, use DISTINCT where needed).

questions.task: Return rate % by Region (join to customers), worst first.
questions.answer:
SELECT c.Region,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)*100.0/COUNT(*), 2) AS return_rate_pct
FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.CustomerID=c.CustomerID
GROUP BY c.Region ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC;

questions.task: Count of orders on deprecated SKUs (not in products).
Top 5 products by net revenue overall, with product name.
questions.answer:
SELECT p.ProductName,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN 0 ELSE o.Revenue END), 0) AS net_rev
FROM orders o JOIN products p ON o.ProductID=p.ProductID
GROUP BY p.ProductName ORDER BY net_rev DESC LIMIT 5;

questions.task: Categories whose net margin % is below the company-wide average margin.
questions.answer:
WITH cat AS (
  SELECT Category,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN 0 ELSE GrossProfit END) AS np,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN 0 ELSE Revenue END) AS nr
  FROM orders GROUP BY Category)
SELECT Category, ROUND(np/NULLIF(nr,0)*100, 2) AS margin_pct
FROM cat WHERE np/NULLIF(nr,0) < (SELECT SUM(np)/NULLIF(SUM(nr),0) FROM cat)
ORDER BY margin_pct;
SELECT CustomerID, MIN(OrderDate) AS first_order FROM orders GROUP BY CustomerID;

WITH m AS (SELECT OrderMonth, SUM(Revenue) rev FROM orders WHERE OrderYear=2023 GROUP BY OrderMonth)
SELECT OrderMonth,
  ROUND((rev-LAG(rev) OVER (ORDER BY OrderMonth))/NULLIF(LAG(rev) OVER (ORDER BY OrderMonth),0)*100, 1) AS mom_growth_pct
FROM m ORDER BY OrderMonth;

questions.task: Top 2 brands by revenue within each category.
questions.answer:
WITH b AS (
  SELECT o.Category, p.Brand, SUM(o.Revenue) rev,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.Category ORDER BY SUM(o.Revenue) DESC) rn
  FROM orders o JOIN products p ON o.ProductID=p.ProductID
  GROUP BY o.Category, p.Brand)
SELECT Category, Brand, ROUND(rev,0) rev FROM b WHERE rn<=2 ORDER BY Category, rn;

questions.task: Distinct customers who ordered in BOTH 2022 and 2024.
questions.hint: Return a single COUNT. INTERSECT the 2022 customer set with the 2024 set, then count.

questions.task: Dedupe customers to one row per ID (latest JoinDate); return rows_removed and rows_kept (in that order).
questions.hint: One row, two columns: rows_removed then rows_kept. Use ROW_NUMBER() per CustomerID by JoinDate DESC; rn>1 are removed, rn=1 are kept.
